newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel bonds close higher in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: Israel bonds close higher in quiet trading.

text.p: Israeli bonds closed higher on Thursday in quiet trading unaffected by the Bank of Israel's expected announcement on its key lending rate for May at the end of the trading day, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon -- issued for four years): +0.14 pct to 105.53
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 to 104.42

"Trading was mixed with a tendency to rise," said Doron Zur at Sahar Securities. "No one is expecting a lot from the announcement (on interest rates). If there will be a cut in rates it will be insignificant."
The Bank of Israel announced on Thursday after the trading day that it was leaving unchanged at 13.9 percent its key lending rate for May.

"Trading was quiet. It is a holiday and there wasn't much trading," said a trader at one of the financial companies. "The CPI-linked bonds traded mixed with a positive trend. Demand was up especially for the CPI-linked bonds with a changing interest rate," she said.
"The expected announcement on interest rates is not affecting the market because the market does not believe there will be a significant cut in the rates," she said.
Trading hours were reduced on Thursday for the intermediate days of Passover.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
